classes.name: General elections to the House of Representatives
classes.name_en: General elections to the House of Representatives
classes.locator: https://www.legislation.govt.nz/act/public/1993/0087/latest/whole.html (Parts 1, 6, and 7; s 191 and Schedule 2: allocation of list seats by the Sainte-Laguë formula)
classes.note: First past the post in single- and multi-member electorates from 1853 to 1993 (second ballots in 1908 and 1911; four Māori electorates from 1868); mixed-member proportional representation since 1996, with a party vote for 120 seats less overhang, a 5 percent or one-electorate threshold, and electorate seats by first past the post in general and Māori electorates. Unicameral since the Legislative Council was abolished on 1 January 1951. Terms run three years from the return of the writs (Constitution Act 1986 s 17) and an election may be called early. The archive holds 2002-2023 from the Electoral Commission's results (2017-2023 by voting place, 2002-2014 party votes by electorate). Contest and seat counts for 1996-2023 come from the Electoral Commission's overall result tables; counts before 1996 wait for the Commission's history tables (dates and turnout from 1853, and seats won from 1890), which elections.nz withholds from scripted requests.

cadence.vacancy_rule: By-election for an electorate seat (Electoral Act 1993 s 129); the next candidate on the party list for a list seat (s 137)

access.evidence: Per-election CSV statistics (overall summary, electorate, and voting-place party and candidate votes) for 2002-2023; the archive's nz.ec packages were built from these files. The host answered HTTP 403 to cloud sessions on 2026-11-17 and 2026-11-20.

classes.name: Sovereign, Governor-General, and Prime Minister
classes.disposition_reason: The Sovereign is hereditary; the Governor-General is appointed by the Sovereign on the Prime Minister's advice (Letters Patent 1983, clause II), and the Prime Minister and ministers are appointed from the House. No executive is elected by voters.

classes.name: Legislative Council
classes.disposition_reason: Members were appointed by the Governor for life and from 1891 for seven years; the elective scheme of the Legislative Council Act 1914 never came into force, and the Council was abolished from 1 January 1951.

classes.name: Judges
classes.disposition_reason: Judges are appointed by the Governor-General on the Attorney-General's advice (Senior Courts Act 2016); none is elected.

classes.name: Party candidate selection
classes.locator: https://www.legislation.govt.nz/act/public/1993/0087/latest/whole.html (s 71: registered parties must follow democratic procedures in selecting candidates)
classes.disposition_reason: Parties select electorate candidates and rank their lists under their own rules; the state runs no primary and publishes no nominating vote.

classes.name: Provincial councils
classes.locator: https://www.legislation.govt.nz/act/public/1986/0114/latest/whole.html (s 26 and Schedule 1: repeal of the New Zealand Constitution Act 1852, which set up the elected provincial councils)
classes.disposition_reason: Returns survive only in the provincial government gazettes and newspapers of the day; no official body publishes them as a register or data, and Papers Past refused scripted requests.

classes.name: Provincial superintendents
classes.locator: https://www.legislation.govt.nz/act/public/1986/0114/latest/whole.html (Schedule 1: repeal of the New Zealand Constitution Act 1852)
classes.disposition_reason: Each province's electors chose its superintendent directly; the returns survive only in provincial gazettes and newspapers, with no official register or data.

classes.name: Regional council elections
classes.finest_note: Councillors are elected by constituency, including Māori constituencies; candidate votes are declared per constituency by each council.
classes.note: Eleven regional councils (Auckland Regional Council too until 2010), elected triennially by postal vote, by first past the post or single transferable vote as each council resolves (Local Electoral Act 2001 ss 27-33). Canterbury's elected councillors were replaced by commissioners from 2010; seven were elected again in 2019 and a full council in 2022. Māori constituencies since 2004 (Bay of Plenty).

classes.name_en: Licensing trusts and other elected trusts
classes.note: Members of the licensing trusts (16 in 2019, from Invercargill, 1944, onward) and of a few other statutory trusts (Masterton and Greytown Trust Lands, Hutt Mana, West Coast Development, Montfort Trimble) are elected with the local elections, by ward or at large.

cadence.administered_by: Each local authority's electoral officer, under the Local Electoral Act 2001 (postal voting)
cadence.locator: https://www.legislation.govt.nz/act/public/2001/0035/latest/whole.html (s 10: triennial general elections on the second Saturday in October)
cadence.vacancy_rule: By-election, unless the vacancy arises within 12 months of the next triennial election (ss 117-118)

access.platform: Each council's electoral officer (declaration of results)
access.evidence: Every council's electoral officer declares the result with each candidate's votes (Local Electoral Act 2001 s 86) and posts it on the council's own site, mostly as PDF; no national compilation of candidate votes exists.

CSV and XLSX for 2013, 2016, 2019, 2022, and 2025 (the 2013 release also carries 2007 and 2010), fetched with HTTP 200 on 2026-11-17: electors, voters, turnout, candidates, and members elected per ward, constituency, and subdivision; licensing trust turnout and candidates. Candidate votes are not in it.

dates.note: Licensing trust elections from the first trust (Invercargill, 1944), triennially with the local elections since 1989; not yet counted.

classes.name: County, borough, city, and town district elections
classes.name_en: Councils and mayors before the 1989 reform
classes.disposition_reason: Results were declared by each of some 200 territorial bodies and survive only in their minutes and in newspapers; no official compilation exists, and the national local statistics start in 1989.

classes.name: Hospital and area health board elections
classes.name_en: Hospital boards and area health boards
classes.disposition_reason: Elected hospital boards (and the partly elected area health boards of 1983-1991) declared their own results; they survive only in board records and newspapers, with no official register.

classes.name: Harbour, power, catchment, and other board elections
classes.disposition_reason: Harbour, electric power, catchment, drainage, road, and similar boards declared their own results; no official compilation exists.

classes.name: School board elections
classes.disposition_reason: Parent representatives on each of some 2,500 state school boards are elected by that school's parents, not by a public electorate, and each school runs and keeps its own election.

classes.name: Iwi, Māori trust board, and Māori land trust elections
classes.disposition_reason: Iwi authorities, Māori trust boards, and land trusts elect under their own deeds and rules for their own members; these are not public elections. Māori political representation in Parliament is through the Māori electorates of the house class.
